verdict.rationale: Twilio's docs reference an Authy API and SDKs for common web languages, so the product does have its own documented programmatic surface. However, Twilio's own page says the API is closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated, so a new AI-native user cannot actually adopt it. Verify v2 is a separate successor product and earns no credit here. Missing for 10: an API open to new users, detailed endpoint/reference documentation in evidence, any API for driving the authenticator app itself (tokens, devices), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: So you don't have to use the Authy API directly to integrate two-factor authentication into your app, we provide an SDK for common web languages.
we provide an SDK for common web languages. If your language is supported, it's the fastest way to get started.
The Authy API is now closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated in the future.
